engagement_background.objective: Create rapid, measurable procurement cost savings by leveraging enterprise-wide purchasing power across indirect and clinical support spend categories in order to improve APDerm’s EBITDA and support its private-equity value-creation plan amid inflationary, pandemic-impacted market conditions.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Strategic sourcing of more than 10 indirect spend categories over two phases. Phase 1 targeted 7 categories representing ~US$11 million in annual spend (Employee Benefits, Medical & Office Supplies, IT Hardware/Software, Telecom, Courier, Small Parcel). Phase 2 added categories such as Billing, Janitorial, IT Managed Services, Temp Labor, Copiers/Print, Uniforms, bringing total addressed baseline to US$6.3 million. Categories with limited savings potential (e.g., Waste Management) or recently renegotiated contracts were excluded.
constraints_challenges: Fragmented, decentralized supply base created through multi-site growth and acquisitions
Limited spend visibility and multiple disparate contracts across locations
Inflationary environment and COVID-related global supply-chain disruptions driving rising costs
Need to minimize business disruption and maintain service levels; preference to keep incumbents where possible
Supplier line-item usage data often unavailable, requiring Treya to contact vendors directly and work with sample data
Aggressive 3–5-month timeline per phase to meet private-equity value-creation milestones
Requirement for APDerm to cease parallel sourcing activity and route all supplier communications through Treya

procurement_environment.data_availability: AP spend data (~US$43 M) exported from internal systems plus scattered supplier contracts; no central contract repository; detailed usage data obtained from vendors case-by-case.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Inconsistent vendor naming and incomplete historical line-item data; multiple locations and systems resulted in scattered, non-standardized information that required cleansing and supplementation from suppliers.

extraction_sources: Agreement/Procurement Cost Reduction Services Agreement_APDerm_12.11.20 - signed.pdf
extraction_notes: Operating model and maturity inferred from statements describing ‘fragmented supply base’, ‘decentralized purchasing’, and lack of spend visibility.
Scope figures taken from Opportunity Assessment (US$11 M across 7 categories) and Case Study (US$6.3 M baseline over two phases).
Data challenges and prohibition on parallel sourcing extracted from Services Agreement sections 3.2.1-3.2.3.
